assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model identified a single, simple mechanism (interlayer tunnelling producing vanishing Dirac velocity and flat bands at a magic angle), and the 2018 experiments showed correlated insulators and superconductivity. This is the clean theory-plus-experiment pairing I value, and it opened the moire materials field, which has spread to many platforms.
assessment.attribution: The prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) and the decisive experimental discovery (Jarillo-Herrero group, 2018) are separable and traceable. Eva Y. Andrei's earlier STM and transport work on twisted layers, and the contributions of the MIT students and collaborators, make a three-person configuration contestable.
assessment.maturity: Independent groups have reproduced the correlated phases and the field is very active; recognition is timely. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated, but the flat-band mechanism itself is well established.
uncertainties: Whether the pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene is settled enough that the prize should not wait
Fair weight for Eva Y. Andrei and for earlier twisted-bilayer theory
Whether Bistritzer should be included beside MacDonald, or MacDonald alone given the theory credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the 'magic wavelength' idea with strontium spectroscopy, giving fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic redshift at the millimetre scale and a redefinition of the second. The idea is simple and general, and its payoff is a measurable, quantitative one.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice (2001-2003) and Ye's group drove the precision and many-body (spin-exchange, SU(N)) developments. Two names give a clean allocation, although Hall and Hansch (frequency combs) were already honoured in 2005 and other lattice-clock groups (for example NIST and JILA colleagues) also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories operate lattice clocks with consistent results, and the redefinition of the second is under way. The field is mature and the recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 prize area for frequency combs and with 2012 trapped-ion work could reduce appetite
Credit to others, such as other lattice-clock groups and ion-clock groups, is not captured by the two names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Exact relations that hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium (Jarzynski equality, Crooks relation, Evans-Searles theorem) are rare, surprisingly universal results, and the kind of simple statement about microscopic reversibility that I find compelling. They have been verified in single-molecule pulling and electronic experiments and underpin stochastic thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Evans and colleagues (1993 fluctuation theorem), Gallavotti and Cohen (1995, not on this list), Jarzynski (1997) and Crooks (1999) form a connected chain. The supplied credit omits Gallavotti and Cohen, which makes any three-person split open to dispute about who first identified the principle.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmations (RNA hairpin pulling, colloidal particles, single-electron boxes) are independent and extensive. The theory is stable, but the impact is mostly on conceptual foundations and biophysics, so a Nobel recognition would be late but not premature.
uncertainties: Missing Gallavotti and Cohen credit in the supplied names
Practical impact may be judged as less than for the experimental candidates
Boundary between statistical physics prize and chemistry or biophysics

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall insulator from spin-orbit coupling in graphene (Kane and Mele 2005) and its realization in HgTe quantum wells (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, Konig et al. 2007) established topological insulators as a new class of matter, with a robust, general mechanism and a huge field following.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the central theory; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental confirmation. Zahid Hasan (3D topological insulators) and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal as well as Zhang and Fu make attribution difficult, and the supplied names include Hasan but not Zhang or Bernevig, which hampers a fair configuration. A three-person set of Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is defensible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by independent groups through ARPES and transport. The 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions, so the field has precedent, and the discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Shoucheng Zhang's death and the exclusion of the BHZ proposal from the credited names
Whether the 3D topological insulator discovery (Hasan, Moore-Balents, Fu-Kane-Mele) should be part of the prize
Overlap with the 2016 topological prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KTHNY theory describes two-dimensional melting as two successive defect-unbinding transitions with an intermediate hexatic phase, a transparent universal mechanism supported by simulations and colloidal experiments. It is exactly the sort of idea that explains a messy phenomenon via a clean model, and complements the 2016 prize for topological defects in 2D.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) developed the theory building on Kosterlitz and Thouless, who are already laureates. Credit is clear and the three names are the natural set.
assessment.maturity: Hexatic phases have been seen in liquid crystals, colloids and simulations, though the nature of melting in simple 2D systems remains partly debated and is system dependent. Recognition would be very late, which weakens timeliness but not merit.
uncertainties: Experimental and numerical evidence for the exact KTHNY scenario is system dependent and sometimes first-order
The 2016 prize may be seen as having already recognised the core of the idea
Committee may regard it as too distant in time

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BPZ construction of two-dimensional conformal field theory gave exact critical exponents and operator content for the 2D Ising and other critical models, with applications from statistical mechanics to string theory and the quantum Hall effect. It is a rigorous and general framework, and from a statistical-physics view one of the central results of the field.
assessment.attribution: The 1984 BPZ paper is the clear locus of credit, with the three authors being the natural set. Contributions of Friedan, Qiu and Shenker, Cardy and others on unitarity and applications are also significant, and the pure-theory character is a recognised obstacle for the prize.
assessment.maturity: Foundational and thoroughly tested against numerics, lattice models and condensed-matter experiments. It is very mature, and the question is whether the committee will reward a theoretical framework with only indirect experimental confirmation.
uncertainties: Distance from direct experiment and the committee's prior reluctance for pure theory
Credit for Cardy, Friedan and others outside the supplied names
Overlap with Polyakov in the AdS/CFT candidate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, with the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and quantum gas microscopes as landmark results. This is a genuine bridge between statistical mechanics and experiment and a platform for studying many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realization (1998), Greiner, Hansch and Bloch observed the Mott transition (2002), and Esslinger realized fermionic Hubbard systems. With five credited names the configuration is crowded, and I would pick the proposer plus the two most closely tied experimental leaders, leaving Cirac and Esslinger out.
assessment.maturity: Mature and replicated worldwide, yet the platform's promise of solving open problems (high-Tc Hubbard physics) is still partly unrealized. Recognition would be reasonable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Crowded credit with Cirac, Esslinger and Hansch not captured in a three-name set
Overlap with the 2001 and 2012 prizes in cold atoms
Whether quantum simulation has delivered results beyond the reach of other methods

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy landscape and funnel picture of protein folding, with minimal frustration, resolves Levinthal's paradox through the statistical mechanics of disordered systems (spin-glass ideas). It is an interdisciplinary physics idea of the kind I find attractive, and it has influenced computational and experimental protein science.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson developed the funnel theory (late 1980s and 1990s), and Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse picture and lattice models. Joseph Bryngelson's role and the contributions of Karplus, Brooks and others make a clean allocation uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The framework is widely accepted and quantitatively used in structure-prediction and coarse-grained models, though much of the field has been transformed by machine learning (AlphaFold). Recognition is mature, but the discipline boundary with chemistry or biology is a concern.
uncertainties: Whether the physics prize can recognize protein folding rather than chemistry
Contribution of Bryngelson and others not in the supplied names
AlphaFold's 2024 chemistry recognition may reduce the sense of urgency
